transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood CSM), Marta Reyes (Novex Head of Procurement), Ethan Cole (Novex CISO), Dr. Asha Kumar (Novex VP Product), Liam O'Neill (Novex Legal)

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, Priya and Samir are here with me. we see Novex on the call, thanks for carving time.
00:12 Marta Reyes: Thanks, Jordan. We're hoping to run through the MSA redlines, DPA clarifications and SLA language — and get a realistic sense of timelines for legal and for a pilot.
00:22 Jordan Lee: Great, that's exactly the agenda, we'll walk through the key items, Priya will cover tech concerns that Ethan raised and Samir will cover compliance artifacts.
00:30 Priya Patel: Hi all, quick note, I'll jump in on VPC and dedicated questions, also on what the pilot looks like from infra side.
00:40 Ethan Cole: Hi. couple quick things — Novex has strict data residency needs for PHI-adjacent data, we also need to understand key management options and whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS or HSM.
00:55 Jordan Lee: Understood. On KMS we do support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private deployments — with integrations for common KMS providers, we'll send the full list. For hosted there's envelope encryption with our KMS but we can discuss bring-your-own-key for Private.
01:18 Marta Reyes: On the MSA, our legal redlines are primarily about indemnity, data processing terms in the DPA, and SLA credits. we also want clearer escalation paths. Liam will share the redlines after this call.
01:35 Liam O'Neill: yes I'll upload redlines to the DocuShare link, expect them by end of day. quick question on versioning — do you allow pinning to model versions and rollback? that's important for us.
01:47 Priya Patel: Yes, customers can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible variants if a model is failing. The console gives per-route rollouts. sometimes the docs call it model catalog, we can point to the exact page.
02:10 Dr. Asha Kumar: From Product side we want to understand latency SLOs for typical LLM calls and how Redwood ensures low tail latency — also how batching impacts our real-time features.
02:22 Priya Patel: Good question. For hosted we publish typical P50/P95 numbers per model, for Dedicated you get more predictable throughput; we also have intelligent batching and KV cache to reduce token cost. tradeoff is batching might increase latency if you allow large queues — we can tune for lower latency for your real-time endpoints.
02:45 Ethan Cole: can you document the exact SLA metrics — uptime, latency guarantees, and credits? Our procurement needs precise wording.
02:52 Jordan Lee: Absolutely, we'll share the SLA spec we use in Enterprise contracts. For Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptime targets and defined credits; for hosted they differ — we'll attach the SLA appendix.
03:10 Marta Reyes: Pricing question — procurement wants a committed pilot price for three months with reserved capacity if we go dedicated. how do we structure that?
03:20 Jordan Lee: Typically we offer a pilot with a monthly commit for Dedicated trial — or Hosted credits for a self-serve trial. For Novex's use case (production-ish latency and PHI constraints) we'd recommend a short Dedicated pilot with a small reserved GPU pool and an autoscale policy for bursts. We'll put pricing options in the worksheet.
03:42 Liam O'Neill: on the DPA — we need specifics on subprocessor list and audit rights, plus the right to require deletion in certain scenarios.
03:52 Samir Gupta: We include subprocessors in the DPA and provide SOC 2 reports; we can provide a list and commit to notify of changes with 30 days' notice. For deletion we have documented processes for data deletion requests — we'll include the flow and timeline in the DPA draft.
04:12 Marta Reyes: also around SSO — we require SAML-based SSO and SCIM provisioning. is that supported?
04:20 Priya Patel: Yes, we support SSO via SAML and OIDC and SCIM for user provisioning. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer IdP. We'll share a short integration checklist.
04:35 Ethan Cole: backup question — if we do Dedicated in a cloud region, where are backups stored and what's the retention? we need to ensure they are within our permitted regions.
04:44 Samir Gupta: backups follow the deployment region; for Private we can do on-prem backups. We'll include specifics in the architecture note and confirm allowed regions.
05:01 Jordan Lee: quick note on termination and data retention clauses — our standard DPA has tiered retention and deletion timelines, we'll highlight those sections to make it easier for your legal.
05:12 Liam O'Neill: thanks. also, do you do penetration testing and can we get summaries or do a joint pen test?
05:20 Samir Gupta: We do annual pentests and provide summaries; joint testing can be discussed for Private deployments under NDA. We'll share the pentest cadence.
05:33 Dr. Asha Kumar: operationally, what's the onboarding timeline if we green-light the pilot? we want to have a pilot running in under four weeks ideally.
05:43 Priya Patel: For Dedicated pilot we typically provision within 5-10 business days once contracts and infra access are set; onboarding + integration work can take another 7-10 days depending on Novex's infra readiness. So four weeks is realistic.
06:05 Marta Reyes: that's good. Procurement's approval path is two internal approvals — procurement and security — and then finance sign-off on the PO. we usually need final contract in two weeks to hit our Q2 timeline.
06:20 Jordan Lee: We'll aim to get redlines back within 3-4 business days and send final pricing worksheet so you have materials for approvers.
06:30 Ethan Cole: on KMS — can Redwood rotate keys with zero downtime? any limitations?
06:36 Priya Patel: Yes, key rotation supported for customer-managed keys, rotation windows are configurable; we'll provide the rotation doc. For HSM-backed keys in Private, rotation is handled by customer KMS.
06:50 Marta Reyes: any limitations on data residency for analytics/telemetry that Redwood collects for monitoring? we need to ensure telemetry doesn't contain PHI.
06:59 Samir Gupta: Telemetry is sanitized by default; we have options to opt-out of certain telemetry and also restrict where telemetry is stored for Private deployments. We'll include the telemetry sanitization note.
07:20 Jordan Lee: a couple of quick clarifying Qs: Marta, is your primary ask to get contract executed or to validate security artifacts first?
07:28 Marta Reyes: both but security validation is the gating item for our CISO. If Ethan signs off on the artifacts quickly, procurement can finish contract review.
07:38 Jordan Lee: OK we'll prioritize sending security docs.
07:45 Priya Patel: For the pilot environment, do you want Redwood to run the Dedicated infra in our cloud account or in Novex's cloud account (Private network connection)?
07:55 Ethan Cole: Novex prefers infra in our cloud account under a dedicated VPC for isolation, so connections will be across VPC peering and we want to manage the KMS.
08:05 Priya Patel: That works — we support customer-managed VPC deployments and can do peering and private endpoints. We'll put together a short network runbook for the pilot.
08:20 Liam O'Neill: about SLA credits there was a clause where our legal wanted a cap lowered, are you flexible?
08:28 Jordan Lee: We can discuss cap adjustments for enterprise deals — for pilot we usually keep standard language but we'll flag it as negotiable in the MSA redlines.
08:38 Marta Reyes: on pricing authority — who will approve discounts? we need a written quote to route to finance.
08:44 Jordan Lee: I'll include the quote in the pricing worksheet and note any approvals required. For material discounts we may need sales leadership sign-off — I'll include that in the timeline.
08:56 Dr. Asha Kumar: small product question — will you support function/tool-calling or structured output in the pilot model? we rely on structured JSON output for downstream systems.
09:06 Priya Patel: Yes we support structured outputs and function calls on supported models; we'll ensure the pilot model has the right capabilities.
09:18 Marta Reyes: ok, next steps recap?
09:22 Jordan Lee: recap: 1) Jordan to send redlined MSA proposal and pricing worksheet by Fri 3/27. 2) Samir to send SOC2, ISO, pentest summary, and DPA one-pager by Wed 3/25. 3) Priya to schedule pilot onboarding for 3/30 and share network/onboarding runbook. 4) Novex to send legal redlines (Liam) and confirm data residency requirements (Ethan) by 3/29.
09:45 Liam O'Neill: noted. I'll get the redlines in.
09:50 Ethan Cole: I'll confirm residency regions and share by next week.
09:55 Jordan Lee: Great. Any other questions?
10:00 Marta Reyes: Not from procurement. thanks everyone.
10:05 Samir Gupta: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.
10:08 Jordan Lee: Thanks, meeting adjourned.
